Method & sources

Vehicle geometry

A detailed artist asset with approximately 1.16 million triangles. Body panels and cabin components have been separated along existing connected surfaces for selection. Materials are adapted for realtime rendering; the source contains no textures. This is not manufacturer CAD, a complete mechanical assembly, or a verified parts catalogue. Cabin view removes the exterior shell for inspection. The engine bay and selected cabin controls are original reference-based reconstructions, with estimated dimensions. They represent visible assemblies, not internal engine mechanisms or an exhaustive catalogue. Opening the bonnet is for inspection only; the flow solver always uses the closed, sealed body.

Potential flow

The mesh is converted into a sealed outer volume on a 136 × 48 × 72 grid. Two converged Laplace solutions are combined for the selected yaw. RK2 integration generates streamlines. Speed scales the field; Cp = 1 − (local speed / freestream)² gives ideal pressure. Samples are taken 75–300 mm outside the visible surface. The coarse grid cannot resolve small details.

This inviscid model does not predict separation, turbulent wake, viscous drag or a real vehicle drag coefficient. Animation speed is reduced for readability.

Viscous study

The local WebAssembly worker uses D3Q19 BGK lattice Boltzmann flow with a static Smagorinsky closure, slip ground and stationary wheels. The grid is too coarse for road-speed Reynolds numbers. The study runs at Re 500 and zero yaw, ramps up from rest, and stops at 2,000 steps. Pressure comes from lattice density. Numerical stability and a wake deficit are checked; this is not validation against a real wind tunnel. No drag or lift coefficients are reported.
